items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: one of my girlfriends name was Joanie Cook

ctx.x: those hotels, then they’d go to San Antonio, to the Gunter, and they appeared at all those hotels and things like that. So that’s why I always wanted to be with Trent, you know because of this, they had a good reputation and they never got stranded like bands were getting stranded there in those days, in big cars and all like that. Of course they had to take the freight elevator when they come to work, they’d look like the guests at the Adolphus Hotel, but when they got on that stand, the first drummer I ever…

He has a large picture of Alphonso Trent’s band. And I remember looking at these musicians, and he’s not one to brag, but he always said he had the sharpest band in the world, because they dressed, they had uniforms, and they were all good looking, very handsome men. And when we lived in Manhattan before we moved to Long Island, one of my girlfriends name was Joanie Cook and her father played for Trent, I mean for Alphonso. And I can remember thinking to myself when I was ten, I must have been around ten, he was…
Treating people’s wives and things — MR: I’ve got a picture here, and see what you can remember about that? 1940?
